figures.alt: The head and hooked uncinate contour remain distinct in reverse. The close-up still has uneven lobulated relief along the inner margin. The matched previous view looks similar at this scale.
figures.caption: Previous delivered sweep and candidate in matched neutral clay.

figures.alt: The saved cut loses raw-label loops and reaches 10.18 mm error against a 3.0 mm limit. Three enclosed mask voids account for much of the difference. Even the filled exterior has a 6.81 mm miss on a small tangential loop.
figures.caption: Frozen source sections and measured contours.

figures.alt: The registered overlay locates the body anterior to the venous landmark. I used the axial scene and reverse surface to follow the head-to-tail curve. The default oblique scene and grayscale alone leave the ends hard to identify.
figures.caption: Saved sweep frame 12 with probe, simulated scan and tissue overlay.

figures.alt: Pancreas CT half-label and interpreted exterior viewed under the same light.
figures.caption: CT reference and reimported surface at matched scale.
